correctness.rationale: An explicit, uniform Gaussian Hilbert–Schmidt norm identity makes t ↦ C_{u+tB(·−u)} analytic in S_2 on ||tB||≤1/4; Cauchy bounds and homogeneous Taylor ranks N_m=binomial(d+m−1,m) yield an absolutely summable trace-class tail O(||B||²). The first derivative factors V B^T W with V*V=G_u and WW*=exp(||u||²)G_u, identifying all d leading singulars exactly. Strict affine contraction gives B=A^n; spectral Jordan asymptotics produce the normalized positive constant. Independent monomial computations and 50 Jordan power checks pass, but they are supplementary to the proof.

residual_risks: General analytic operator-valued map theory might imply first-order trace-class differentiability under analogous assumptions; priority is assessed for the combined explicit displaced Gram and Jordan formula, not generic analyticity.

value.rationale: Quantifies the rate left open by the source qualitative iteration theorem, resolving a natural inverse approximation question at all Schatten levels; the rank-d first variation gives the entire dominant singular spectrum with a quadratic S_1 remainder. Nontrivial Jordan blocks produce sharp polynomial-times-exponential rates with an exact nonnormal/displacement coefficient, with natural limiting cases and an explicit defective two-dimensional example. The facts are not merely special-parameter calculations or restatements of norm convergence.
